environment.kernel: Linux 6.18.57 (version reference only; vendor patch not attested)

method.control: Previous delivered BBR driver with same capture fixture and test-only iteration counter; old dependency lock
method.final: Deadline-driven driver, path-event draining and upgraded DNS/time dependencies
method.bulk: Two CONNECTs in one QUIC connection, 24 paced pieces plus 1 MiB per stream; transfer timing excludes outer handshake and shutdown
method.paired_order: control/final, final/control, control/final for seeds 1/42/2026 within each loss level; no concurrent compilation or analysis
method.relay: TLS-transparent UDP, 20ms each direction, 100Mbit/s serialization, 4MiB bounded queue; seeded independent datagram drops
method.soak: One authenticated duplex CONNECT; 1KiB echo followed by 250ms gap; fixture idle timeout 10s; production default 600s
method.outage: 120-second H3 workloads: 10% random loss plus 2000ms blackout. First pair starts after 1000ms and can affect handshake; separate established-channel pair starts after 10000ms, with wall-clock validation against authenticated channel start/end. Already queued datagrams may still arrive

security.kernel_fix_scope: Host kernel update and boot; application auth/TLS/BBR cannot fix pre-accept TCP UAF

dependency_scan.method: crates.io semver only; Git/vendor sources reviewed separately

excluded: Five early loss/soak smoke captures are not formal benchmark samples
The first 1000ms-offset blackout pair is retained but not used to compare established-channel recovery, because the final handshake overlapped the outage
Repeated-NAT-port experiment failed at the second change; preserved as a documented implementation limitation, not counted as a passing test
limits: Three seeds per loss level do not estimate WAN tail latency or general speedup
No TCP high-loss network emulation, public VPS deployment or fairness study
30/120-second real-network tests and virtual 24h expiry check are not a 24-hour soak
RSS includes server, client, fixture and accumulating capture payloads
Single-CID routing supports tested single NAT rebinding; a second repeated change timed out
No new public GTS/Porkbun issuance, musl build, real DPI recognition rate or kernel exploit test
Two unmaintained transitive dependency advisories remain; Git/vendor reviewed separately from OSV semver queries

method.control: previous 0.6.0 H3 driver with identical current fixture and TCP policy
method.timer_final_cleanup: same timed code; scoped expected deprecation on private OwnedFd registration, preserving forbid(unsafe_code)
method.bulk: two CONNECT streams on one outer connection, each 24 chunks at 4ms intervals then 1 MiB; timed after outer TLS/QUIC handshake until full payload verified, before shutdown
method.passive: original pcap without keylog; TCP type23 lengths include opaque_type, parsed per record tree
method.decrypted: test keylog only; H3 uses separate Retry analysis copy, original preserved
method.tcp_bbr_verification: getsockopt on real listener, inherited accepted socket and Egress; ss lacks algorithm/pacing fields on this kernel

limits: Local experiment, no production VPS change or real WAN TCP BBR benchmark
Kernel lacks prio/netem; UDP relay approximates path only for QUIC, no QUIC/TLS termination
No Chromium proxy-client, public GTS/Porkbun issuance, real DPI recognition-rate or 24-hour load test
No BBR fairness/cross-traffic study; not a BBR-versus-Cubic comparison
Only three batches per performance condition; no p95 inference
JA3/JA4 describe this synthetic client; changing certificates does not remove stack or timing signals
TLS 1.2 certificate chains and ordinary SNI are passively visible; TLS 1.3 certificates encrypted but sizes remain observable
Raw pcaps and test TLS keys excluded from source archive
excluded: cert-smoke*, cert-matrix*, cert-tls12*, bbr-loopback*, cert-check-final preliminary phases
final-relay-delay-1-control startup failed before workload: incomplete Python standard library; rerun as final-shaped-*
initial self-signed non-CA leaf rejected by Validator; no verification bypass
initial inner TLS intermediate-chain fixture omitted chain; fixed before complete final-cert rerun
